$comment: When to use each button variant. The component itself is src/styles/components/button.css, built from Figma "Foundation – UI 2" (Buttons, node 18:3529; component set 23:5203). Shown on the Buttons page and published to public/llms.txt by `npm run tokens`.
intro: Buttons let users initiate an action, acknowledge something, make a choice, or navigate. By default, our buttons are 24px tall, come in two styles (primary and secondary), and can optionally include an icon in front and in back.
rules: Use a <button class="button button--<variant>"> for actions and an <a class="button button--<variant>"> for navigation; never style a <div> as a button.
Use one primary button per view or panel; pair it with secondary buttons for the other actions.
Disable with the disabled attribute on <button> or aria-disabled="true" on links; every variant then shares the same disabled look.
Write labels as short verbs (Save, Delete, Continue), not "OK" or "Click here".
Icons are 16px <span class="button__icon" style="--icon: url(…)"> before or after the label; they take the label's color. Icon-only buttons need an aria-label.

variants.label: Primary
variants.usage: The main action in a view, e.g. Save or Continue. Use one per view or panel.

variants.label: Secondary
variants.usage: Supporting actions next to a primary button, e.g. Cancel or Back.

variants.label: Tertiary
variants.usage: Low-emphasis actions in toolbars, lists and dense UI, where a fill would add noise.

variants.label: Danger
variants.usage: Destructive actions that can't easily be undone, e.g. Delete. Confirm before acting.

variants.label: Success
variants.usage: Positive, confirming actions, e.g. Approve or Publish.
